narrative.overview:
A run is a transit map on a midnight-blue enamel sign. Jobs are stations shaped as pills, the dependencies between them are curved tracks. Anyone who looks reads, without a word of text, what waits on what and where it is stuck. The interface works in Operate mode: it is glanced at for two seconds in passing or read closely while following a run, and the same view has to carry both.

The system is calm and flat. There is exactly one dark theme, no shadows, no gradients and no pure white. Depth comes from four closely stepped blues, structure from fine hairlines. The typeface is Overpass in light weights; all numbers use tabular figures because they keep counting every second. Saturation is reserved for state: six state colors, each with its own drawn icon, are the only things on the surface that glow.

Density follows the task. In compact mode a pill shows icon, name and time; on hover it expands, its neighbors make room and the tracks follow. In detail mode all pills are open. Below the network map sits the machine's load as a history over time, not as a momentary value.
keyCharacteristics: Network map instead of job list: stages from left to right, tracks between the pills.
Dark only, midnight blue; the lightest tone is porcelain blue-grey, never white.
State always twice: color and drawn icon.
Light type (200 to 400), tabular figures everywhere.
Flat: tonal steps and hairlines instead of shadows.
Load history as a line with a faint area below it.

rules.name: The No-White Rule
rules.body: The lightest tone is `ink`. Pure white appears nowhere, not even in icons: on filled state circles the drawing is cut out in `ground`.

rules.name: The Color-Plus-Icon Rule
rules.body: A state never appears as color alone. Each of the six colors has its drawn icon (triangle, check, cross, square, dash, dot); anyone who cannot tell the colors apart reads the icon.

rules.name: The Tracks-Stay-Blue Rule
rules.body: Tracks never carry a state color. They are `track`, dotted `track-open` while the target's turn has not come, and `ink` when the pill at their end is hovered. The state sits at the station, not on the line.

rules.name: The Red-Means-Trouble Rule
rules.body: Red means something needs the user to step in: a failure in the run, full memory, an action that deletes something. Nothing else.

rules.name: The Light-Weights Rule
rules.body: Running text is 300, emphasis 400, nothing above that except the wordmark. The larger the type, the lighter the weight.

rules.name: The Tabular-Figures Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` applies to the whole page. Times keep counting every second; without fixed figure widths pills and columns would jitter.

rules.name: The No-Caps Rule
rules.body: Labels use normal case without letter spacing. All caps and tracking do not occur.

rules.name: The Tonal-Step Rule
rules.body: A surface stands out through the next lighter step and a 1 px border, never through a shadow. The order is fixed: `rail`, `ground`, `surface`, `raised`.

rules.name: The Response-Is-One-Step Rule
rules.body: Hover lifts a surface exactly one step (`surface` → `raised`) and turns its border from `edge` to `track`. Nothing moves from its place.

dos: Do always show state as color and icon at once, with the six fixed pairs.
Do draw dependencies as a curved track from right middle to left middle, 2.5 px, round caps.
Do stack surfaces by tonal steps (`rail`, `ground`, `surface`, `raised`) and frame them with 1 px `edge`.
Do set numbers in tabular figures and right-align them where they stand in columns.
Do show load as history over time, with cap, peak and the start of the run as reference.
Do mark estimates as such ("about", "usual", "rough estimate") and keep them in `muted` or `text`, not highlighted.
Do draw what is open as dashed or dotted and without fill, what is done or running as solid.
Do use `fail-text` for red type and `fail-edge` for red borders; `fail` itself only for filled icons and the warning chart.
donts: Don't use pure white; the lightest tone is `ink`.
Don't add a light theme; the system is dark only (`color-scheme: dark`).
Don't use shadows, gradients or blur.
Don't color tracks in a state color or route them straight or at right angles.
Don't show a run as a job list with status dots in cards.
Don't use one of the glowing state colors (`run`, `done`, `fail`, `cancel`) as decoration or for anything other than its state.
Don't set type heavier than 400 (exception: the wordmark) or letter-space labels in all caps.
Don't use the pill shape for anything other than a job.
